projects.title: Quartiersbüro Schelmengraben
projects.desc:
Repurposing a disused parking structure in Wiesbaden into the Quartiersbüro Schelmengraben serves as a bold statement on architectural recycling. By "breathing" a new, civic life into a rigid concrete shell, the design proves that sustainability isn't just about new materials, but about the reclamation of existing urban mass. The facade is wrapped in a warm, horizontal timber skin, a material choice that immediately shifts the building's identity from a cold utility to an inviting community hub.
The structure’s "active" skin is a study in functional aesthetics. Integrated photovoltaic panels are woven directly into the facade's rhythm, turning the building into a self-sustaining energy generator that powers its own internal transformation. Large, rhythmic glazing replaces former dark voids, flooding the new office spaces with natural light and establishing a visual dialogue with the surrounding parkland. It is a project where ecology and urbanity meet—a quiet, timber-clad beacon that honors the city's green heart while providing a high-performance workspace for the future

projects.title: Alkozai HQ
projects.desc: To break the monotony of the long horizontal site, we introduced vertical brick-textured fins and angled slabs. These elements serve as 'architectural punctuation,' creating a unique visual rhythm that guides the eye toward the primary entrance while providing natural shading to the office windows.

projects.title: Ahmad-yar Lobby
projects.desc:
Luminous ribbons of light serve as a chromatic compass, silently guiding visitors through the lobby's expanse without the need for physical barriers. This overhead sequence creates a sense of effortless momentum, drawing the eye toward the heart of the space while defining a clear, intuitive path. By embedding the circulation logic directly into the ceiling's geometry, the architecture manages the flow of the room through light rather than restriction.
The interior is anchored by the tactile honesty of local stone, used as a rugged sculptural backdrop that contrasts with the sleek, high-gloss surfaces. A monumental, mosaic-clad column stands as a textured pivot point, bridging the gap between the earth-toned flooring and the vibrant, neon-lit canopy. It is a design that celebrates the meeting of the contemporary and the geological, offering a welcoming threshold where the raw materials of the region are refined by modern digital precision.

projects.title: Parametric wall Installation
projects.desc: Parametric design transforms a static wall into a kinetic sculpture, where a series of rhythmic, vertical fins create a sense of fluid movement within the stillness of a bedroom. By varying the depth and curvature of each dark slat, the installation "opens" and "closes" as the viewer moves through the space, revealing a hidden, warm glow that pulses from within.

projects.title: Al-Haramain Tailoring
projects.desc: Al-Haramain Tailoring is a study in tactile elegance, where the warmth of craftsmanship is reflected in the architecture itself. The facade is anchored by the rhythmic use of thermowood panels, creating a deep-set, textured frame that invites clients into a world of bespoke detail.

projects.title: A Second Home for Students
projects.desc:
This award-winning proposal, titled "A Second Home for Students," reimagines the hillside of Kabul University’s Engineering Faculty as a living laboratory for architectural inspiration. As the 1st place winning design, it moves away from rigid institutional grids in favor of an organic, biomorphic landscape that breathes with the natural topography of the site.
The design is a study in social and physical well-being. By carving out intentional, designated zones for both female and male students, the project ensures a sense of comfort and belonging within a shared academic ecosystem. A rhythmic network of jogging tracks and pedestrian arteries weaves through the terraced greenery, transforming the commute between classes into a revitalizing experience. Hand-rendered with markers to maintain the soul of the initial creative spark, this landscape is not just an addition to the campus—it is a sanctuary where the next generation of architects can find clarity, health, and community.

projects.title: Moraa Information Desk
projects.desc:
Exercise in architectural transparency and accessibility, designed to serve as the welcoming face of the Moraa Education Institute. The structure is conceived as a "light pavilion," where crisp white planes and large horizontal apertures dissolve the boundary between the administrative interior and the verdant campus landscape.
The design utilizes a minimalist, cantilevered language to create a sense of weightlessness. By elevating the desk on a gentle grassy berm and integrating deep-set window awnings, we’ve created a space that feels both open to the community and naturally sheltered from the elements. It is a quiet but firm statement on the importance of clarity in education, providing a luminous point of guidance that respects the natural rhythm of the existing trees.

projects.title: Mental Health Hospital
projects.desc:
Healing is rarely a straight line. By adopting a fluid, organic form, this hospital mirrors the ebb and flow of the human mind, providing a sanctuary where the architecture breathes alongside its occupants. It is a bridge between the precision of the digital age and the soft rhythms of the natural world.
A groundbreaking proposal for Kabul Mental Health Hospital that replaces the traditional, clinical "box" with a fluid, biomorphic landscape. As the first organic-style public facility in the country, the design uses parametric architecture to create a sense of continuous movement, reflecting the complex and non-linear journey of healing.

projects.title: Sal-Saal Furniture Showroom
projects.desc: This project is an exploration of contemporary commercial identity that pays homage to traditional roots. Centered in the heart of Kabul, the facade serves as a bold, modern canvas where the "Shamshat" (Islamic geometric star) acts as the primary architectural anchor—a symbol of light and guidance that transitions the building from a mere storefront into a cultural landmark.

projects.title: 7012 Tower
projects.desc:
This design is an exploration of fortified transparency, where the rugged permanence of local natural stone meets the delicate requirements of urban privacy. The facade acts as a protective "stone screen," utilizing deep architectural recesses and horizontal apertures to shield the interior from direct sightlines while still framing curated views of the Kabul skyline.
The lighting strategy is cinematic and rhythmic, turning the building’s evening presence into a sequence of glowing "voids" and "solid mass." By highlighting the texture of the stone against the sleek, illuminated bands of the balconies, we’ve created a structure that feels heavy and grounded by day, but light and permeable by night. It is an architecture that respects the street-level boundary while reaching upward for light and air.

projects.title: Bahar Residence
projects.desc:
This multi-family residence in Kabul is an exercise in sculptural staggering, where the traditional domestic boundary is reimagined through a series of interlocking volumes. By shifting the floor plates, we’ve created a "vertical landscape" of private terraces and deep-set balconies, providing each family with a dedicated outdoor sanctuary while naturally shading the interiors from the intense Afghan sun.
The facade is a dialogue between texture and void. The warmth of the red brick and rugged stone accents provides a grounded, tactile connection to the earth, while the crisp white planes and large-format glazing reach toward the light. It is a design that prioritizes visual privacy and communal rhythm, using the "box-in-box" geometry to define individual living units within a singular, cohesive architectural statement.

projects.title: Shamal Mall
projects.desc: This project is a visionary intervention for the city center, designed to act as a catalyst for a new era of urban dignity. Conceived as a landmark that bridges the gap between high-density commerce and private sanctuary, the building reinterprets neoclassical proportions for a modern skyline, creating a "vertical city" that feels both grounded and aspirational.

projects.title: Mumtaz-Mahal Wedding Hall
projects.desc:
Mumtaz Mahal Wedding Hall is an exploration of palatial symmetry and rhythmic light. The design seeks to create a sense of awe through a highly articulated ceiling—a tiered landscape of gilded coffers and illuminated grids that defines the hall’s vast volume while maintaining a sophisticated, human-centered glow.
The space is anchored by a monumental neoclassical framework, where arched bays and slender pilasters provide a structured, rhythmic backdrop to the vibrant energy of the celebrations. By utilizing a highly reflective flooring material, the intricate ceiling motifs are mirrored below, effectively doubling the visual height and creating a seamless, immersive environment of light and gold.

projects.title: Mini Kitchen
projects.desc: The spatial strategy focused on vertical layering. By integrating overhead bulkheads with recessed lighting, we’ve defined the kitchen's 'ceiling' independently from the rest of the apartment, creating an intimate, 'carved-out' feel that maximizes the impact of the natural light from the adjacent window

projects.title: Office of the Minister of Economy
projects.desc:
This design for the Minister’s office is a study in institutional identity, where the solemnity of governance meets the warmth of Afghan heritage. The space is anchored by a deep, tiered ceiling—a "black mirror" that creates an illusion of infinite height—bringing a necessary sense of gravity and scale to a room built for critical decision-making.
The material palette creates a bridge between worlds; modern wood paneling and charcoal velvets provide a sleek, contemporary frame, while the vibrant crimson rug and intricate geometric fretwork behind the desk act as cultural anchors. It is an environment that balances the heavy weight of responsibility with the light of transparency, expressed through clean horizontal lines and recessed illumination.

projects.title: Master Bedroom
projects.desc:
This project is an exercise in spatial layering within a compact footprint. In this master bedroom, we’ve utilized dark, architectural framing to "carve out" functional zones, creating a room within a room that feels both protective and expansive.
The design relies on the contrast of textures: the ruggedness of the exposed brick wall against the high-gloss reflective ceiling panels and soft, organic wallpaper. By integrating a mirrored overhead element, we’ve effectively doubled the perceived volume of the space, allowing the abundant natural light from the floor-to-ceiling windows to bounce and fill the room. It is a sanctuary that balances the rigor of modern cabinetry with the warmth of a lived-in retreat.

projects.title: Luxury Guest-Room
projects.desc: An exploration of grandeur and symmetry, where every element is choreographed to create a sense of timeless elegance. By utilizing a Neoclassical framework, the space is divided into rhythmic bays defined by gilded pilasters and ornate coffered ceilings, grounding the vast scale in human-centric proportions.

projects.title: Spinosaur Bench
projects.desc: The Spinosaur Bench is a study in how rigid geometry can mimic organic rhythm. Inspired by the striking dorsal sail of its namesake, this parametric piece uses a series of repeating, vertical fins to create a sense of fluid movement through a static form.
